label: Thomas Aquinas, Sententia libri…: Things… supports No two distinct things depend for their…
note: In V Metaph. lect. 13 n. 18 states that dependence between a prior and its posterior is one-way (priora non dependent a posterioribus, sicut e converso). The premise generalizes this to every pair of distinct beings one of which depends for its being on the other. That needs the unstated step that whatever x depends on is prior to x; without it, the passage leaves open mutual dependence between things not ordered as prior and posterior (for example correlatives, or Lewisian counterfactual dependence).
